newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: METROPAC SAYS TO EXPAND, BETTER NET SEEN.
newsitem.headline: METROPAC SAYS TO EXPAND, BETTER NET SEEN.

text.p: Diversified concern Metro Pacific Corp (MPC) said on Monday it would continue to expand its main businesses to allow it to sustain the high income growth registered in the first half of the year.

"MPC continues to expand in accordance with a strategy of planned diversification, designed to create a platform for sustainable long-term growth in recurring net income," MPC president Napoleon Nazareno said in a report.
The company earlier reported a 156 percent leap in first-half net profit, excluding other income, to 420.4 million pesos from a year earlier.
Unaudited consolidated net income totalled 574.5 million pesos against 393 million.
"The group continues to investigate new opportunities, and the prospects for 1997 and the future are very encouraging," Nazareno added.
Total assets rose to 96.2 billion pesos as of June this year, up from 21.4 billion as of December last year, following the acquisition of an additional stake in the Bonifacio Land Corp last June.
Metro Pacific now has about 56 percent of Bonifacio which is jointly developing a 214-hectare lot at the edge of Manila's Makati business district.
The joint venture property firm, Fort Bonifacio Development Corp, reported a 2.7 billion peso income before tax in the first six months of the year.
It said new residential and office buildings will be completed and ready for occupancy in three years' time. An entertainment centre will be opened by early 1998.
The subscribers' base of its telecom affiliate Smart Communications Inc has risen 19 percent in the second quarter of the year.
Metro Pacific recently announced it would raise its stake in Smart to majority control from the present 28 percent.

"The strong earnings growth from Smart, and the opportunities for further expansion and development in the future outside MPC's traditional businesses, are anticipated to enhance MPC's earnings per share," the company statement said.
Metro Pacific also said it would continue to restructure its packaging units. It recently consolidated its corrugated carton production in just one plant.
Metro Pacific likewise allayed fears of possible financial difficulty arising from the recent de facto devaluation of the peso.
It said it has limited foreign currency exposure, most of which is convertible to equity.
"As a consequence, the extent of exchange losses for the year associated with the recent depreciation of the peso is presently anticipated to be limited," a company statement said.
It added that it can easily absorb the cost of imported raw materials and foreign currency expenses.
